Article 73

The family in efforts to protect women's rights plays a role in:
a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights within the household; andc. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 29

1. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 21 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on violence prevention and handling;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; ande. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 76 (1) The Head of the PD that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection must submit a report on the implementation of women and child protection programs to the Regent.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically once (1) every 6 (six) months.

Article 77 (1) The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.

2. In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a PD in accordance with its duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for the policy of women and child protection programs in the Region.

Article 32

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for the victim.
2. Social reintegration is intended so that:a. women victims of violence can resume their social life; andb. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Paragraph 3

Social Field

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 53

1. Regional Governments are obliged to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains an optimal degree of health from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;

Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.

c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; ande. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.

2. In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a PD in accordance with its duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for the policy of women and child protection programs in the Region.

Article 53

1. Regional Governments are obliged to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains an optimal degree of health from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, child victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of human trafficking.
3. Regional Governments, communities, families and parents are obliged to ensure that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 28

1. Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:a. not imposing any religion or belief; andb. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim.
3. Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
4. Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of consultants from the Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Agency, Officers of the Religious Affairs Office, religious leaders, who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on violence prevention and handling;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; ande. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.

Article 76 (1) The Head of the PD that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection must submit a report on the implementation of women and child protection programs to the Regent.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically once (1) every 6 (six) months.

Article 77 (1) The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.

2. In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a PD in accordance with its duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for the policy of women and child protection programs in the Region.

CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 2

Every woman and child has basic rights as a human being that must be protected, promoted, upheld and fulfilled in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 23. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

1. Employers who employ women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while at the workplace.

3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB and 07.00 WIB are obliged to:a. provide nutritious food and drinks; andb. maintain decency and security while at the workplace.
4. Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB and 05.00 WIB.

Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 23. PUG Focal Point is an OPD apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 34

1. Employers who employ women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while at the workplace.
2. Employers are obliged to place female workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.
3. Employers are obliged to fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

1. CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 2

Every woman and child has basic rights as a human being that must be protected, promoted, upheld and fulfilled in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 35

1. Female workers/laborers under the age of 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB and 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB and 07.00 WIB are obliged to:a. provide nutritious food and drinks; andb. maintain decency and security while at the workplace.
4. Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB and 05.00 WIB.

Article 73

The family in efforts to protect women's rights plays a role in:
a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights within the household; andc. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 75

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on violence prevention and handling;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; ande. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 76 (1) The Head of the PD that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection must submit a report on the implementation of women and child protection programs to the Regent.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically once (1) every 6 (six) months.

Article 77 (1) The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.

2. In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a PD in accordance with its duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for the policy of women and child protection programs in the Region.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 32

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for the victim.
2. Social reintegration is intended so that:a. women victims of violence can resume their social life; andb. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Letter b Sufficiently clear Letter c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information disclosed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Letter e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Letter f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled women/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school teachers.

Letter j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative.

Letter k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Letter l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 34

1. Employers who employ women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while at the workplace.
2. Employers are obliged to place female workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.
3. Employers are obliged to fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 35

1. Female workers/laborers under the age of 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB and 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB and 07.00 WIB are obliged to:a. provide nutritious food and drinks; andb. maintain decency and security while at the workplace.
4. Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB and 05.00 WIB.
